failed_conditions.quote: A second potential problem is that stereo_image_proc is not running at frame rate. You can see that stereo_view is getting less than one disparity image for every five image pairs. ... stereo_view keeps a queue of size 5 (by default) on each input topic, which means the left/right image messages may drop off the queues by the time their matching disparity image arrives. The solution is to increase ~queue_size.

probably they are not synchronized - that is, left and right image time stamps don't match up exactly. All the image_pipeline nodes assume exact synchronization for stereo (the ideal case) by default. ... You need to do the same with stereo_view, as the warning message recommends.

notes: Eligibility agreed (stop_step 6, PAIR, topic). Verified via Stack Exchange API: question 29632 body carries the stereo_view WARN log and 'Synchronized triplets: 0'; accepted answer by Patrick Mihelich carries both diagnoses and the fix command. FAILED-CONDITION 0 ERROR: the spec classes the queue-size/rate problem as 'element_removed_or_renamed', but nothing is removed or renamed. The disparity publisher runs below frame rate (fewer than one disparity per five image pairs) and the size-5 queue drops the images before the disparity arrives — a delivered-rate shortfall. Correct class is rate_shortfall. Condition 1 (exact-vs-approximate timestamp sync) class 'other' is a fair fit; agreed. Loudness: the node's own periodic run-time WARN is a run-stage message, not a build/connect/activate tooling diagnostic, so silent_documented/run is defensible and agreed. Resolution 'recommended' (accepted answer proposes the fix; no re-run shown) agreed.
